subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote successful compaction completion into a single authoritative reconciliation boundary for all compaction-derived session state, or keep the current narrow counter/token repairs and track remaining mismatches individually?
rationale: Current source proves the existing repair is intentionally narrow, but choosing field ownership across status tokens, memory flush bookkeeping, auth-profile rotation, and recovery paths is an architecture/product boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Define a bounded reconciliation boundary
options.body: Make successful compaction completion the owner for monotonic updates to session fields that are semantically derived from compaction success, with focused tests for each moved field.

options.title: Keep narrow repairs only
options.body: Leave the current count/token paths as-is and require each remaining mismatch to be filed and fixed as an independently reproduced bug.

options.title: Split before implementation
options.body: Break this broad follow-up into smaller maintainer-owned issues for status tokens, memory flush state, auth override rotation, and recovery semantics before code work starts.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded reconciliation boundary
recommendation.body: Make successful compaction completion the owner for monotonic updates to session fields that are semantically derived from compaction success, with focused tests for each moved field.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and PR metadata put the newest ownership of the relevant session-state files with vincentkoc.
